To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

IgG anti-M.leprae antibody activity increases with the progression of leprosy from BT to LL, that the IgM anti-M.lepraa antibody activity in indeterminate lepromatous is significantly higher than in the control, and that the IgA anti-M.lepraea activity is higher in indeterminate than in the control but with considerable overlap between these two groups.

IgA and IgM anti-M.leprae antibody activity is increased in leprosy compared with healthy controls, that the increase in IgA and IgG anti M. lepræ activity in leprosy is more pronounced than in the IgM activity, that the IgM anti M. lepra activity is higher in indeterminate than in healthy individuals and that there is no difference in the IgG activity in indeterminate leprsy and healthy controls.
IgM anti-M leprae activity is higher in untreated leprosy than controls, but decreases after 10 years of MDT.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of serological assays for the diagnosis of leprosy and with the study of the immune response of the leprosy patient to M. lepraemurium.
the use of immunoglobulin specific antibodies to M leprae as markers in the study of the pathogenesis and the development of serodiagnosis of lepros.
the development of methods to detect M. lepr ae in the skin of patients with leprosy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IgA anti-M leprae is the most useful assay for serodiagnosis of lepros

the IgM anti-M.leprae assay is the most suitable for sero-diagnostic use, while the IgA assay is of value in the evaluation of the humoral immune response in untreated leprosy and in monitoring the effect of treatment.
IgM and IgA assays are more suitable for the diagnosis of leprosy, while the IgG assay may have more use in monitoring treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a combination of IgM and IgA anti-M leprae activity is the most sensitive and specific test for the diagnosis of leprosy, while IgG activity may be useful in monitoring the course of the disease and the effect of treatment.

the IgA and IgM assays are useful in detecting leprosy patients in the lepromatous group, and in the indeterminate group, whereas the IgG assay is of limited value in the indeterminate and lepromatOUS groups.

the IgG anti- M. lepr ae assay is the most suitable for serological studies of the humoral immune response in leprosy, whereas the IgM and particularly the IgA anti-M.leprae assays may be useful as screening tests for leprosy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IgM anti-M leprae assay is the most promising for use in the sero-diagnosis.

a combination of IgM, IgA and IgG assays may be used for sero-diagnoses in the leprosy spectrum, but that the IgM assay may be the most valuable for sero-diagnostically discriminating between leprosy and other diseases in endemic areas.
IgA and IgM assays are useful for screening purposes, whereas IgG is more useful as an indicator of the degree of exposure to M. lepra.
